# `silk/json_output`

<!-- Generated by packages/compiler/scripts/generate-documentation.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Profiles: `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-no-libc`, `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-no-libc`.

Allocation-free JSON string escaping and formatting through the ambient Writer.

## When to use

Use [`JsonOutput`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6a736f6e5f6f75747075743a3a4a736f6e4f7574707574) when writing a JSON string, validated number, or container punctuation.
[`JsonOptions`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6a736f6e5f6f75747075743a3a4a736f6e4f7074696f6e73) chooses compact or indented output and bounds container depth.

## Details

Each operation writes directly to `Writer`. A failed write may leave an accepted prefix; no
operation flushes the provider or allocates JSON-owned storage.

## Examples

### Configure two-space indentation

```silk
import silk.json_output { JsonOptions }
import silk.usize

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let options = JsonOptions.indented(2)
  return usize.toI32(options.indent)
}
```

Import as `JsonOutput` with `import silk.json_output { JsonOutput }`.

Public declarations: 2.
